```{r options, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5, fig.align = "center", dpi = 96)
old_options <- options(digits = 3, width = 90)
```

A sentence embedding is only as reproducible as the model that computed it.
Two analyses that both say they used "all-MiniLM-L6-v2" can disagree if one
downloaded the model a year later, after the repository was updated, or if
a file was truncated in transit. The choice of model also shapes the
result: models differ in the languages they were trained on, in the length
of text they read, and in the size of the vectors they return, and each of
these limits what an analysis can ask of the embeddings.

`sbert` treats the model as part of the method. Each supported model is
pinned to an immutable revision of its Hugging Face repository and to the
size and SHA-256 hash of every file, downloads happen only when asked for,
and every file is verified before it is used. This guide covers the
registry of pinned models and how to choose among them, installing the
runtime and a model, the cache in which models are kept, scripts that run
without a person to answer a prompt, and models outside the registry.

```{r setup}
library(sbert)
```

## Data

The data of this guide is the registry of pinned models, returned by
`models()`. Reading it needs no download and no network.

- **`model`:** the name passed to `load_model()`, `encode()` and the topic
  verbs.
- **`dimensions`:** the length of each embedding vector.
- **`max_tokens`:** the longest input the model reads, in its sub-word
  tokens; longer inputs are truncated.
- **`languages`:** the languages the model was trained for.
- **`size_mb`:** the download size in megabytes.

```{r registry}
models()
```

```{r registry-numbers, include = FALSE}
registry <- models()
```

The registry pins `r nrow(registry)` models. They return vectors of
`r with(registry, min(dimensions))` to `r with(registry, max(dimensions))`
dimensions and take from `r with(registry, min(size_mb))` MB to
`r format(with(registry, max(size_mb)), big.mark = ",")` MB of disk. The
default, `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, returns 384 dimensions, reads 256 tokens and
takes 90.9 MB.

## Which model fits the corpus?

Three properties decide the choice: the languages of the texts, their
length, and the cost the analysis can bear. The language comes first: an
English model embeds text in other languages poorly, and texts in two
languages that mean the same thing are close only in a multilingual model.

```{r multilingual}
subset(models(), languages != "English")
```

Of the pinned models, `r nrow(subset(registry, languages != "English"))`
are multilingual. The two `paraphrase-multilingual` models read
128 tokens, about a long sentence; `multilingual-e5-small` reads 512. For an
English corpus, length is the next question.

```{r long-inputs}
subset(models(), max_tokens >= 512)
```

Of the pinned models, `r nrow(subset(registry, max_tokens >= 512))` read
512 tokens or more, and `nomic-embed-text-v1.5` and
`jina-embeddings-v2-small-en` read 8,192, more than a research abstract needs.
`potion-base-8M` lists 1,000,000 because it has no window at all: it is a
static model that looks up a vector for each token and averages them,
without a neural network. It is the smallest model in the registry, needs
no ONNX Runtime, and replaces the transformer with a table lookup, but
averaging ignores word order, so
"the teacher helped the student" and "the student helped the teacher" get
the same vector. A long-window model is one answer to long documents;
splitting them into sentences, covered in the [guide to segmenting long
documents](segmenting.html), is the other, and it works with every model.

`models(detail = TRUE)` adds the technical settings that `encode()` applies
automatically.

```{r detail}
subset(models(detail = TRUE),
       select = c(model, pooling, prefix, engine, license))
```

`pooling` is how token vectors become one text vector: the mean of all
tokens, or the vector of the first (`cls`) token, as each model was
trained. `prefix` is text that two models expect before every input
(`"query: "` for `multilingual-e5-small`, `"search_document: "` for
`nomic-embed-text-v1.5`); `encode()` adds it, so the caller passes the text
alone. `engine` separates the transformer models (`onnx`) from the static
one. The licenses are Apache-2.0 or MIT. The full Hugging Face id and the
pinned revision are in the columns `id` and `revision`.

Dimension has a cost: memory and k-means time grow with it. A corpus of
100,000 texts at 1,024 dimensions takes `r 1e5 * 1024 * 8 / 1e6` MB as a
matrix of doubles (8 bytes per value), against `r 1e5 * 384 * 8 / 1e6` MB at
384. A larger model is worth its cost when a
comparison on the corpus, for example with `compare_topics()`, shows it
separates the themes better (see [choosing the number of
topics](choosing-topics.html)).

## What does a first run need?

A transformer model needs the native ONNX Runtime, which the `onnxr`
package installs on request. The model's files are then downloaded once.
Neither step happens during installation or loading of `sbert`, and neither
is run in this guide.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install_runtime()                         # once per machine
model_download("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")        # once per model
model <- load_model("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
embeddings <- encode(c("A first sentence.", "A second one."), model)
```

`install_runtime()` passes `cuda` to `onnxr::onnx_install()`: `FALSE` asks
for the portable CPU runtime, `TRUE` for CUDA where it is supported, and
`NULL` (the default) detects which. `model_download()` fetches only the
files that are missing or fail verification, writes each to a temporary
file, checks its size and SHA-256 hash, and moves it into the cache only if
both match. `load_model()` never downloads: it loads files already in the
cache, verifies them again (`verify = TRUE`), and stops with an error of
class `sbert_model_not_installed` when a file is missing,
`sbert_cache_invalid` when one fails verification, and
`sbert_runtime_missing` when a transformer model is loaded without ONNX
Runtime. The static `potion-base-8M` is loaded without the runtime.

Verbs that take a model name, such as `encode(text, model =
"bge-small-en-v1.5")`, load it themselves and keep it for the rest of the
session. If it is not installed, an interactive session asks once whether
to download it, giving the size and license.

## Where are the models kept?

All models live in one cache per user, outside any project, at the
location R designates for the package's cached files.

```{r cache-dir}
cache_dir()
```

`cache_dir()` returns the path from `tools::R_user_dir("sbert", which =
"cache")` and creates nothing. Inside it, each pinned model has a directory
named after the model and its revision, so two revisions can never be
mixed. `model_status()` lists the files a model needs and checks them.

```{r status}
subset(model_status(model = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"),
       select = c(file, exists, valid, expected_bytes, actual_bytes))
subset(model_status(model = "potion-base-8M"),
       select = c(file, exists, valid, expected_bytes, actual_bytes))
```

```{r status-numbers, include = FALSE}
default_status <- model_status(model = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
```

The default model consists of `model.onnx` and `tokenizer.json`; the static
model of an embedding table (`model.safetensors`), a tokenizer and a
configuration file. On the machine that built this page no model is
installed, so every file is reported missing (`exists` is
`r with(default_status, unique(exists))`) and invalid. `valid` is true only
when the file has the pinned size and hash; `model_status()` only reads, so
calling it is safe at any time. The `path` column, left out here, gives
where each file is expected.

```{r size}
cache_size()
```

`cache_size()` is the number of bytes used by all files under the cache,
here `r cache_size()` because nothing has been downloaded. Models are kept
until they are removed, and `model_remove()` deletes the directory of one
pinned model; other models and custom models are untouched.

```{r remove, eval = FALSE}
model_remove(model = "all-mpnet-base-v2")
```

Every one of these functions takes `cache_dir`, so a project can keep its
models elsewhere, for example on a shared drive, by passing the same path
to `model_download()`, `model_status()` and `load_model()`.

## Scripts that run unattended

A script run with `Rscript`, a scheduled job or a knitted report has no
one to answer the download prompt. In such a session a missing model is an
error of class `sbert_model_not_installed`, never a silent download.
There are two ways to allow the download.

```{r unattended, eval = FALSE}
# Either install explicitly, once, before the analysis runs ...
model_download("all-MiniLM-L6-v2", quiet = TRUE)

# ... or allow this script to download any model it needs.
options(sbert.download = TRUE)
embeddings <- encode(c("A first sentence.", "A second one."))
```

With `options(sbert.download = TRUE)`, a verb that needs a missing model
calls `model_download()` itself, with the same verification as an explicit
download. The explicit call is the better choice for a shared or published
analysis: the script then states which models it depends on.

## Models outside the registry

`load_custom()` loads any public Hugging Face repository that ships an ONNX
export of an encoder and a `tokenizer.json`. The result is an `sbert_model`
like those from `load_model()`, so `encode()`, `topics()` and every other
verb accept it.

```{r custom, eval = FALSE}
gte <- load_custom("thenlper/gte-small")
embeddings <- encode(c("A first sentence.", "A second one."), gte)

# Pin a revision, and state settings that cannot be detected
gte <- load_custom("thenlper/gte-small",
                   revision = "<commit hash>",
                   pooling = "mean", max_length = 512)
```

A custom model is trusted on first use. On the first call, `load_custom()`
resolves the repository's current revision (unless `revision` is given),
detects the pooling from the repository's Sentence-Transformers
configuration and the maximum length from `sentence_bert_config.json`
(512 when that file is absent), downloads the two files, and records their
sizes and SHA-256 hashes in a local manifest. It stops with an error when
the pooling cannot be detected and is not given. A later call with the
same `revision` reads the manifest, verifies the files against it, and
does not use the network. A later call without `revision` first asks
Hugging Face for the repository's current revision; if the repository has
changed, that revision is downloaded and recorded as a new model, so an
analysis that must not change pins `revision`. The
files are kept under `custom/` in the cache directory, one directory per
repository and revision, and `model_remove()` does not delete them. It needs
the `jsonlite` package.

The difference from a pinned model is who vouches for it. The registry's
hashes and settings were fixed by the package; a custom model's were
recorded from whatever the repository held on first download, and the
package makes no claim that its embeddings match the original
implementation. Passing `revision` makes the analysis reproducible; checking
a few embeddings against the reference implementation, as the [verification
guide](verification.html) describes for the default model, makes it
trustworthy.

## Which call for which task

- See the available models and their settings: `models()`,
  `models(detail = TRUE)`.
- Set up a machine: `install_runtime()` once, then `model_download()` for
  each model the analysis uses.
- Check an installation without loading it: `model_status()`; disk use:
  `cache_size()`; free space: `model_remove()`.
- Run a script unattended: `model_download()` beforehand, or
  `options(sbert.download = TRUE)`.
- Use a model not in the registry: `load_custom()`, with a pinned
  `revision`.
- Encode faster: `load_model(threads = "auto")` or the static
  `potion-base-8M` (see [parallel and high-throughput topic
  modeling](parallel.html)).

```{r reset, include = FALSE}
options(old_options)
```
